title: How to Book Group Flights: A Step-by-Step Guide for 10+ Travelers
metaTitle: How to Book Group Flights for 10+ People (Step-by-Step)
metaDescription: Learn how group flight bookings work: deposits, name deadlines, seat blocks and how to get the best group airfare for 10 or more travelers.
content:
Booking flights for a big group is very different from booking a single ticket. Prices, payment rules and name deadlines all work differently. This guide explains how group air travel works and how to get the best fare for your party.

What counts as a group booking?

Most airlines define a group as 10 or more passengers traveling together on the same flights, in the same cabin, on the same dates. Groups of this size can be priced by the airline's group desk rather than through the normal public fare system.

Why not just buy 10 tickets online?

  • Prices climb as you buy. Public fares are sold in buckets. The first few seats may be cheap, but the price often jumps before you finish buying for the whole group.
  • Everyone pays upfront. Individual tickets must be paid in full immediately.
  • Names are fixed. Changing a traveler on a regular ticket is usually expensive or impossible.

A group contract solves all three problems: one fare for every seat, a deposit to hold the space, and names submitted later.

Step 1: Gather your trip details

Before you ask for a quote, know your departure city, destination, preferred dates (and how flexible they are), the approximate number of travelers and the cabin you want.

Step 2: Request quotes early

Airlines open group inventory up to about 11 months before departure. Asking 3 to 9 months ahead gives the best choice of flights, especially for summer and holiday travel.

Step 3: Compare the full terms, not just the price

When comparing group quotes, check the deposit amount, when the balance is due, the name deadline, how many seats you can release without penalty, and the change and cancellation rules.

Step 4: Pay the deposit and collect names

Once you accept a quote, the deposit locks your seats and fare. Use the time before the name deadline to confirm who is traveling and collect payments.

Step 5: Ticketing and travel

After final names and payment, tickets are issued for everyone. Request seats, special meals and any assistance before the day of travel.
